t: Minimum Operations to Write the Letter Y on a Grid
o: In an odd n×n grid, the Y consists of the two diagonals from the top corners down to the center, plus the center column below the center. Every Y cell must share one value a, every non-Y cell another value b ≠ a. Count how many Y cells hold each value 0/1/2 and likewise for non-Y cells; then for each ordered pair (a, b) with a ≠ b the cost is (Y cells not equal to a) + (non-Y cells not equal to b). Try all 9 pairs and take the minimum. Example 1: Y cells are (0,0),(0,2),(1,1),(2,1) and the rest form the background; choosing a=1, b=0 costs 3.
k: Membership in the Y is purely geometric: r ≤ half and on a diagonal, or r > half and c = half.
With only 3 values, brute-forcing all 9 (a, b) assignments is trivial.
Cost formula: (ycnt - cntY[a]) + (ocnt - cntO[b]) for a ≠ b.

a.i: Classify each cell as Y or background and tally value frequencies per group. Since the optimal assignment only depends on these six counts, testing all pairs (a, b), a ≠ b, in O(9) gives the answer.
s: Tally yv[v] and ov[v] for v in 0..2, plus totals yc and oc.
For each a ≠ b in {0,1,2}², compute (yc - yv[a]) + (oc - ov[b]).
a.t: O(n²) — one classification pass plus O(9) enumeration.

w: Get the geometric predicate right: the center cell belongs to both diagonals but must be counted once, and the vertical arm is strictly below the center. A common bug is using r >= h for the vertical arm, double-counting the center. Follow-up: generalize to k colors or a different letter shape — the count-and-enumerate framework stays identical.
